best_for: Engineers, students and programmers who type calculations faster than they click buttons and want precise results with a running history.

points.title: Answers as you type
points.text: Results and autocomplete appear while you type the expression, so you rarely press equals. Each pane keeps its own history you can scroll back through.

points.title: Fifty digits of precision
points.text: It calculates to 50 digits and ships with over 140 functions and 390 constants, plus units and your own variables and functions.

points.title: Handy for programmers
points.text: Hex, binary and octal, bitwise operators, IEEE 754 tools and a bitfield tool make it useful for low-level work.

points.title: What 1.2 changed
points.text: Version 1.2.0 starts much faster on Windows, lets you set your own keyboard shortcuts, adds style presets and a system light or dark mode, and makes number formats follow your chosen decimal and grouping marks.

points.title: Intel Macs are left out
points.text: The macOS build listed here is for Apple silicon only and needs macOS 14 or later. Windows gets a machine-wide x64 installer.

points.title: Free, open source, verified Flatpak
points.text: SpeedCrunch is free under the GPL. The Flathub build is verified as published by the project and runs on x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 4 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
